# Exact KKT, finite martingale dual, and actual cap loads for the residual program

This note gives an exact finite dual and geometric contact identities for
`candidate 3869d933360d8c9c`.
It does not assert an unconditional bound R_1<=(1-gamma_q)M. That bound
can fail even for genuine covering caps on a no-heavy-fiber family whose
actual depth is above the requested threshold.

## 1. Primal data and KKT system

Let P={p_1,...,p_N} be the actual positive integer bases, q>=1 the
intrinsic dimension, and e_i>=0 the sampled best residual roots after
unions of at most t original caps. The attained program is

    R=min sum_i h_i^q,
    h_i>=e_i,
    h_j>=h_i+g_i.(p_j-p_i)  (i!=j).                       (1)

All h_i are nonnegative. Vectors g_i live in the direction space of
aff(P). Fix an attained optimizer (h,g). Define

    s_i=q h_i^(q-1) if q>1,
    s_i=1           if q=1.                              (2)

There are multipliers lambda_i>=0 and mu_ij>=0 (i!=j) satisfying

    lambda_i(h_i-e_i)=0,                                 (3)
    mu_ij[h_i+g_i.(p_j-p_i)-h_j]=0,                      (4)
    sum_j mu_ij(p_j-p_i)=0,                             (5)
    lambda_i=s_i+out_i-in_i,                            (6)

where out_i=sum_j mu_ij and in_i=sum_j mu_ji.

Here is a direct justification of multiplier existence. The constraints
form a finite polyhedron. At its minimizing point, a direction satisfying
all active linearized inequalities is feasible for a sufficiently small
positive step, since every inactive inequality has positive slack.
Therefore the objective gradient is nonnegative on that cone of feasible
directions. Finite Farkas separation puts its negative in the cone of the
active constraint gradients, giving nonnegative multipliers and (3)--(6).
The finite Farkas alternative and closed-cone proof are given in Section 2
of the cited program source. For q>1 use the differentiable convex
extension sum(h_i)_+^q off the feasible polyhedron; for q=1 use the linear
function sum h_i. These have precisely the gradients (2). Thus zero
sampled heights do not require an unproved differentiability convention.

Multiplying (4) by its multiplier and using (5) gives

    sum_ij mu_ij(h_i-h_j)=0.

Multiplying (6) by h_i and summing consequently proves

    sum_i lambda_i e_i=sum_i lambda_i h_i
         =sum_i s_i h_i=qR.                              (7)

Also sum lambda_i=sum s_i, and their first moments agree by (5).

## 2. Explicit finite martingale coupling, without an existence black box

There is a nonnegative matrix pi_ij with

    sum_j pi_ij=lambda_i,
    sum_i pi_ij=s_j,
    sum_j pi_ij p_j=lambda_i p_i.                        (8)

For q>1 first remove zero-height nodes. If h_i=0, (4)--(5) imply
sum_j mu_ij h_j=0, so every positive outgoing edge goes to another
zero-height node. Summing (6) over their set Z gives
sum_Z lambda_i=-sum_(i outside Z,j in Z)mu_ij. Hence all these quantities
vanish. On Z the remaining flow is conservative and has row barycenters.
Thus

    sum_(i,j in Z) mu_ij |p_j-p_i|^2
      =sum_(i,j in Z) mu_ij(|p_j|^2-|p_i|^2)=0,

where row barycenters removed the cross term and conservation removed the
last sum. Since distinct indices are distinct points, every remaining
mu_ij there is zero. Zero-height nodes therefore have no flow or lambda
mass, and s_i=0. They may be ignored in (8). If all heights are zero, the
zero matrix already proves (8).

On the remaining nodes s_i>0; for q=1 this holds on every node from the
outset. Put

    a_i=s_i+out_i,
    T_ij=mu_ij/a_i,
    D_ii=s_i/a_i.

Every row sum of T is at most 1-delta for some delta>0, because the
finite set of ratios s_i/a_i is positive. Consequently

    N=(I-T)^(-1)=sum_(m>=0)T^m

converges. Define

    pi_ij=lambda_i N_ij D_jj.                            (9)

Equation (6) says a=lambda+aT in row-vector notation, hence lambda N=a.
Also T 1+D 1=1, and the row barycenter equations give
T p+D p=p, coordinatewise. Multiplication by N proves N D 1=1 and
N D p=p. These three identities prove exactly all statements in (8).
Thus the coupling is an explicitly defined finite absorbing-chain matrix;
no unproved infinite transport assertion is invoked.

For every convex function phi on conv(P), (8) and Jensen yield

    sum_i lambda_i phi(p_i)<=sum_j s_j phi(p_j).           (10)

Moreover this coupling stays on supporting faces of the optimal threshold.
The quantities

    h_j-h_i-g_i.(p_j-p_i)

are all nonnegative by primal feasibility. Their pi-weighted sum is zero,
by (7)--(8). Hence

    pi_ij>0  ==>  h_j=h_i+g_i.(p_j-p_i).                 (11)

Every positive-lambda source is an obstacle contact h_i=e_i by (3).
Destinations with s_j>0 need not be obstacle contacts; (11) does not say
e_j=h_j.

## 3. The exact finite concave dual

For q>1 put q'=q/(q-1) and c_q=(q-1)q^(-q'). Then

    R = max_pi [sum_ij pi_ij e_i
                   -c_q sum_j (sum_i pi_ij)^q'],         (12)

where pi_ij>=0 and each row obeys

    sum_j pi_ij(p_j-p_i)=0.                              (13)

No prescribed row sums or column sums are imposed in (12). For q=1 the
corresponding exact dual is

    R = max_pi sum_ij pi_ij e_i,
    pi>=0, (13), sum_i pi_ij=1 for each j.                (14)

To prove weak duality, set lambda_i=sum_j pi_ij and s_j=sum_i pi_ij.
For any primal feasible h, Jensen and h>=e give
sum lambda_i e_i<=sum s_j h_j. For q>1, Young's inequality gives
s h<=h^q+c_q s^q' for every h,s>=0; this is the exact conjugacy identity
obtained by maximizing s h-h^q over h>=0. This proves that the objective
of (12) is at most the primal objective. For q=1 the fixed column sums
give the same conclusion directly.

The coupling constructed in Section 2 attains equality. Its column sums
are s_j=q h_j^(q-1), its row masses are the KKT lambda_i, and (7) gives
sum lambda_i e_i=qR. Also c_q sum s_j^q'=(q-1)R. This proves (12),
including attainment; (14) follows from (7) with q=1. Independently, the
dual feasible set in (14) is compact. For (12), the objective tends to
minus infinity as total pi mass tends to infinity, because its negative
term has degree q'>1 while its positive term grows at most linearly.

Equations (12)--(13) are a finite martingale dual, not a restatement in
terms of unspecified convex test functions. All its variables and
constraints are explicitly finite.

## 4. Actual cap-mass loads carried by contact multipliers

For every i with lambda_i>0 choose an original cap subset J_i, |J_i|<=t,
attaining the local residual minimum e_i. Let

    c_i^*=H_q(K_(p_i) intersect union_(a in J_i) H_a)
          =V_i-e_i^q.

For q>1 define rho_i=lambda_i/(q e_i^(q-1)) at positive-lambda sources,
and rho_i=0 elsewhere. This denominator is positive: Section 2 proved
lambda_i=0 whenever h_i=0, while positive lambda requires e_i=h_i.
For q=1 define rho_i=lambda_i, including zero-residual contacts. Then

    R=sum_i rho_i e_i^q,
    sum_i rho_i V_i-R=sum_i rho_i c_i^*.                  (15)

There is no 0^0 convention in these definitions.

For each original cap a put

    L_a=max{rho_i: lambda_i>0 and a in J_i},

with maximum zero for an empty index set. Since a union is bounded by
the sum of its original cap masses, (15) gives the concrete inequality

    sum_i rho_i V_i-R
       <=sum_a L_a mu(H_a).                              (16)

Indeed, after expanding each selected union, the contribution of cap a
at contact bases is at most L_a times its full actual mixed mass. In
particular, if all original caps have mass at most B, then

    B sum_a L_a >= sum_i rho_i V_i-R.                    (17)

These loads retain which original caps are used at which contacts. They
are not presumed to have sum at most k, and the weighted volume in (17)
is not presumed at most M. Such assertions would be additional numerical
claims, not KKT consequences.

For a genuine covering cap family, ordinary intrinsic Grünbaum at each
fiber centroid additionally gives e_i^q<=(1-gamma_q)V_i for t>=1. Hence
R<=(1-gamma_q)sum_i rho_i V_i. This last estimate is on the CONTACT-WEIGHTED
volume; replacing it by (1-gamma_q)M is unjustified. Equations (16)--(17)
are the promised inequalities against actual global cap masses.

## 5. Midpoint geometry of positive obstacle contacts

Let Q={p_i:h_i=e_i>0}. If p_a,p_b in Q have the same parity, put
p_c=(p_a+p_b)/2. Then p_c belongs to P and to Q, and

    h_c=e_c=(e_a+e_b)/2.                                 (18)

For a direct proof, every residual subset J has positive endpoint
q-volumes, since its residual roots are at least e_a,e_b>0. Their
Minkowski average lies in the actual residual section at the integer
midpoint. The maximum integer fiber dimension is q, so the endpoint
direction spaces must coincide; otherwise the average would have dimension
greater than q there. Intrinsic Brunn--Minkowski gives
f_J(p_c)^(1/q)>=(e_a+e_b)/2 for every J. Taking the finite minimum gives
e_c>=(e_a+e_b)/2. Convexity of the optimal threshold and its sampled
majorization give the reverse chain

    e_c<=h_c<=(h_a+h_b)/2=(e_a+e_b)/2.

This proves (18). Convexity also makes the threshold affine on the whole
segment [p_a,p_b]: equality at an interior point of a segment of a convex
function forces equality on that segment.

If a residual subset J is active at p_c, all inequalities in

    e_c=f_J(p_c)^(1/q)
       >=[f_J(p_a)^(1/q)+f_J(p_b)^(1/q)]/2
       >=(e_a+e_b)/2=e_c

are equalities. Thus the SAME J is active at both endpoints. Its residual
closures are homothetic when q>=2, by the equality case of ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski, and their midpoint Minkowski average equals the residual
closure at p_c. Equality of volume plus convex containment justifies the
last assertion. For q=1 these are intervals and exact interval-length
equality gives the same Minkowski identity directly. In either case their
ordinary centroids average exactly. Residuals may be nonclosed, but taking
closures leaves their positive q-volumes and centroids unchanged.

The same conclusion holds for a martingale row whose every positive target
is a positive obstacle contact. Choose a residual subset J active at its
source. Its target roots are at least their contact heights, whose row
average is the source height by (11). The source root is that same height;
weighted Brunn--Minkowski forces equality throughout. Consequently J is
active at every target and the residual centroids satisfy the row
barycenter identity. This assertion is conditional on the targets being
positive contacts; general destinations in (8) need not satisfy it.

## 6. What the dual does not supply

The exact dual, weighted cap loads, and midpoint identities do not prove
the sharp mixed-integer budget. In particular the following substitutions
are invalid without new hypotheses:

* replacing sum rho_i V_i by M;
* replacing sum_a L_a by the occupied parity count;
* assuming every martingale destination is an obstacle contact;
* extending residual-root BM through an EMPTY target residual section.

A zero residual measure at a target does mean that the corresponding
chosen union captures its full q-measure, whether that residual is empty
or only lower-dimensional. More generally, for any chosen J and 0<=eta<1,

    sum_{p: H_q((U_J)_p)<=eta V_p} V_p
       <= mu(union_(a in J)H_a)/(1-eta)
       <= |J|B/(1-eta).                                  (19)

This is an exact available payment against actual cap budgets. It does
not manufacture a nonempty residual needed by a barycentric BM argument.
Retaining those distinctions is necessary for any later arithmetic use
of the finite martingale dual.
